Full reveal of Ellis's final notebook entry / unsent status report, layered onto whichever primary ending played

END-1.name: Triumphant Launch
END-1.narrativeSummary: The batch (or both batches, if BIG-01 was handled well) is released cleanly and the NHS contract is confirmed. Mike E. privately admits the project nearly broke Ellis in the same seat — an offer of succession, not just closure.
END-1.tone: Earned, warm, quietly bittersweet about Ellis

END-2.name: Pyrrhic Victory
END-2.narrativeSummary: Contract secured, but the cost is visible — Daniel notes the margin is thinner than promised, and the team is visibly depleted in the control-room scene.

END-3.name: Contract Lost, Lesson Learned
END-3.narrativeSummary: The batch is fine but arrives too late — a competitor wins the contract. Mike E. is disappointed but respects the player's honesty, leaving the door open for a future project.

END-4.name: Batch Rejected — Redemption Arc
END-4.narrativeSummary: The first batch is rejected on a quality technicality, but the strong documentation trail means the root cause is found fast and a second batch succeeds within weeks.

END-5.name: Batch Rejected — Project Paused
END-5.narrativeSummary: The batch is rejected and the evidence trail is too thin to diagnose quickly. The Board pauses the programme pending external review. The player is reassigned — an explicit mirror of Ellis's fate.

END-6.name: Politically Undermined
END-6.triggerCondition: Mike E. Trust OR Camille Trust at Cold band by Act 6, regardless of Delivery Score
END-6.narrativeSummary: The physical build succeeds but the political battle is lost — a rival executive uses the friction to have the player quietly moved off the project just before launch, exactly as happened to Ellis.
END-6.tone: The game's core thesis made explicit

END-7.name: The Whistleblower Ending
END-7.triggerCondition: Stakeholder Goodwill falls to its lowest band at any point in Act 4
END-7.narrativeSummary: Unresolved external concerns (e.g. an unanswered social media safety claim) escalate into a formal external investigation that overtakes the project's own timeline.

END-8.name: Ellis Grant's Understanding
END-8.triggerCondition: Epilogue — unlocked whenever all 6 notebook fragments are found; layers onto whichever primary ending played
END-8.narrativeSummary: The player reads Ellis's final, unsent status report. Ellis wasn't a bad PM — they carried the exact same pressures the player just survived, alone, for far longer. The core lesson lands explicitly: PM isn't about perfect answers, it's about informed decisions under uncertainty, made by people who don't always agree with you.
